text.text: Under this containment structure, full mediation of the Matching-Gf relation by the WMCDE factor is the expected outcome, and it carries no information about which construct is more fundamental.
This interpretation rests on assumptions that deserve explicit statement: 1.
Common signal dimension.
The perceptual precision captured by matching and the perceptual component of WMC task performance reflect the same latent dimension.

For WMCDE, which uses the same stimuli and response format as matching, this holds by design even if precision were feature-specific; for WMCPM it additionally requires perceptual precision to generalize across content domains.
Gf-irrelevant task-specific variance.
Matching-specific variance -motor adjustment noise, criterion setting, encoding strategies -is unrelated to Gf.
If part of it predicted Gf, matching would retain unique Gf variance beyond WMCDE.
Latent-level testing.
The residual tests are performed on latent variables.
With fallible manifest scores, unreliability of the WMCDE measures alone would produce apparent partial mediation.
No suppression.
Regressing matching on the WMC factors does not induce suppression between maintenance variance and matching-specific variance.
The observed residual correlations are all positive, showing no suppression signature.
Additivity.
Representational quality and maintenance combine approximately additively in producing Gf variance; strong interactive combinations could produce patterns the decomposition would misattribute.

Under these assumptions the decomposition makes a falsifiable joint prediction: WMCPM and WMCDE should retain Gf-relevant variance beyond Matching, whereas Matching should retain no Gf-predictive variance beyond the WMC factors.
The first half was supported decisively in every group (smallest BF10 = 8.12).

The second half was not decisively supported in any group: the Bayes factors were inconclusive in Study 1 younger adults (BF01 = 0.64), Study 1 older adults (BF01 = 0.43), and Study 2 (BF01 = 1.07, residual r = .17, 95% CrI [.01, .33]); in no specification did evidence for absence reach moderate strength (largest BF01 = 1.89; see below).

A decisively positive matching residual (BF10 > 3) would have refuted strict containment; the observed residuals were small and their Bayes factors inconclusive, though their 95% CrIs lie mostly above zero -leaving open a small unique matching contribution.
text.formatted: A decisively positive matching residual (BF10 > 3) would have refuted strict containment; the observed residuals were small and their Bayes factors inconclusive, though their 95% CrIs lie mostly above zero -leaving open a small unique matching contribution.

text.text: Controlling for WMCDE alone in Study 2 indeed left a credible residual (see below).
We therefore describe the structure as approximate rather than strict containment.Alternative parameterizations of the reverse model.
The reverse residual test can regress Matching on WMCDE, on WMCPM, or on both jointly.

The main text controls matching for WMCDE -its maintenance-enriched counterpart -in both Study 1 age groups, and for WMCPM and WMCDE jointly in Study 2, where the two memory factors are separable (latent r = .59); in Study 1 younger adults they are strongly correlated (latent r = .84), so the joint regression weights are not interpretable there -though the residual Matching-Gf correlation, the quantity of interest, remains so.

The two WMCPM-based variants for Study 1 younger adults yield the same conclusion: regressing Matching on WMCPM alone -the latent-variable analogue of the prior WMC-only mediation tests(Jastrzębski et al., 2021; Troche et al., 2014)  -gives a residual Matching-Gf correlation of r = .19 (BF01 = 1.89), and the two-predictor model gives r = .19 (BF01 = 1.84), both inconclusive.

In Study 2, the single-predictor WMCPM model gives r = .21 (BF10 = 3.31), close to the two-predictor estimate, at the boundary of the inconclusive band.Controlling for WMCDE alone in Study 2, in contrast, leaves a clearly credible residual: r = .29, 95% CrI [.12, .46], BF10 = 22.38.

The single colour DE task does not fully account for the shared variance of Gf with the two matching tasks (color and luminance matching), whereas Study 1's DE factor -which spans the same feature spaces as Matching (colour and orientation) -leaves only an inconclusive residual.

This result should not surprise us: Mediation is expected to be complete only when the set of DE tasks samples the perceptual variance of Matching at least as broadly as the Matching tasks themselves.
The quantity of interest -the residual Matching-Gf covariance -is an algebraic function of the latent correlations and is stable across parameterizations that control the same factors.
Robustness transfer.

The correlation, residual, and reverse residual models are reparameterisations of the same covariance structure, so the reverse-model semipartial is an algebraic function of the latent correlations among Matching, the WMC factors, and Gf.

The robustness of these correlations to rank-normalisation (Robustness Check: Rank-Normalized Observed Variables) and to the pure-Gf specification (Sensitivity Check: Older Adults with a Pure-Gf Factor) therefore extends to the reverse residual correlations without re-fitting.
